what: every measured section re-scored against upstream's OWN bf16 gradient error instead of against float64. The bf16 column is computed here from arm4; the device column is each section's own measured figure with its source named. Nothing new was run.
why: D70 established that the 2.0e-02 mass-weighted bar against a float64 reference is missed by upstream's own training dtype (bf16 autocast, 2.9x outside on the device arm's scope). A bar the model's authors do not meet is the wrong yardstick for 'reproduce OpenFold3 training'. This table asks the useful question instead: how does our deviation compare to the recipe's own?

the_reframing.headline: 49.4 % of the model deviates from float64 by NO MORE than upstream's own training precision does, and essentially the entire failure is ONE module: the diffusion transformer at 141.6x. Scored against float64 the campaign reported 54 % outside the bar; scored against the recipe's own floor it is one bad module and a long tail already at parity.

THE_CAVEAT_THAT_LIMITS_ALL_OF_IT.statement: both columns are distances from the SAME float64 reference. Two deviations from a shared reference do not order each other: our 7.865e-03 beside bf16's 6.2532e-02 does NOT establish that we agree with bf16's gradient to 6e-02. The errors could point in different directions and our distance FROM BF16 could exceed both.
THE_CAVEAT_THAT_LIMITS_ALL_OF_IT.what_is_established: our deviation from the float64 ideal is no larger than the recipe's own deviation from it, on 42.2794 % of the model. That is real and useful.
THE_CAVEAT_THAT_LIMITS_ALL_OF_IT.what_is_NOT_established: that we reproduce upstream's bf16 TRAJECTORY. 'Reproduce OpenFold3 training' in the strict sense is agreement with what their step actually computes, which is a device-vs-arm4 comparison.
THE_CAVEAT_THAT_LIMITS_ALL_OF_IT.the_measurement_that_would_close_it: compare our device gradient tensors DIRECTLY against arm4's bf16 gradients rather than both against float64. arm4 is on disk at of3t_refprec/run/arm4_bf16_autocast/grads_f64.pt; what is missing is our device gradient TENSORS -- the device arm published rel/r/cos per tensor but not the gradients. One re-run of device_gradient.py writing the tensors closes it.
THE_CAVEAT_THAT_LIMITS_ALL_OF_IT.this_is_the_shared_subtrahend_rule: two diffs against one reference do not order each other; an A/A arm is needed. It is on the campaign's own standing list and applies squarely here.

provenance: computed 2026-09-20 pass 173 by of3t-orchestrator, CPU only, no device opened. bf16 column from arm4_bf16_autocast/grads_f64.pt against bundle_min_043/grads_f64_043.pt, aggregated by top-level section over all 4,170 tensors. Device column is each section's own published figure, source named per row -- three come from their own rows at their own scopes rather than from the 547-tensor diffusion array, and mixing sources is why every row carries its provenance.
